extracted.subtask_description: A printed specimen sheet showing the same body copy set in multiple typefaces, point sizes, and lead (line-spacing) options to evaluate appearance, legibility, and character shapes for book typography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens of Types in Use
rubrics_metrics.description: SPECIMENS OF TYPES IN USE — the sheet presents multiple specimens of the same text set in different faces, sizes, and settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The repeated heading and layout indicate the page's purpose: to compare how a single passage looks when set in different typefaces, sizes, and leadings. Use these specimens to judge overall suitability of a face for body text and display at different sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface classification (MODERN / OLD STYLE / MONOTYPE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section headings label faces as MODERN, OLD STYLE, and MONOTYPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categorical labels identify stylistic/technical families of type; compare characteristics associated with each family (contrast, serif shape, overall color) when choosing a face for a project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point size (five, six, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, fourteen, eighteen points, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit point-size labels appear (e.g., 'FIVE POINT NO. EIGHTY-THREE', 'SIX POINT NO. THIRTY-ONE', 'EIGHTEEN POINT NO. EIGHT').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimens show the same passage at each labeled point size so the reader can evaluate legibility, texture, and appropriateness of the size for body text, captions, or display use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaded vs Solid (line-spacing / leading treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each specimen is marked '[Solid]' and often also '[Leaded]'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows the same type set with no extra leading (Solid) and with added leading (Leaded). Use to assess effects of line spacing on readability, color (gray value), and overall page texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body-text exemplar (same running text across specimens)
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuous historical passage (beginning 'When thoughtful Greeks like Polybius saw the fall of Carthage and of Corinth...') is used as the exemplar text in every specimen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a realistic multi-sentence passage allows assessment of word spacing, hyphenation, line breaks, paragraph shape, rhythm, and overall readability in each face/size/leading combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character set and glyph samples (vowels, consonant sets, numerals, punctuation, special combos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Short glyph rows and sequences are shown (e.g., 'AEIOU', 'aeiou', '1234567890', assorted punctuation, ligature-like sequences and letter pairs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specimens let the reviewer inspect individual letterforms, numerals, punctuation, kerning/fit of common pairs, and the presence/shape of special glyphs or small-caps/figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display capitalization and emphasis (all-caps lines / emphasized lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain lines are set in all caps or emphasized (e.g., ‘IT WAS NOT THE FIRST TIME…’, other uppercase blocks and headings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes examples of how the face performs in display or emphasized settings — useful for judging weight, spacing, and suitability for headings or emphasis in addition to body text.
